proposed.author: Taha Echakiri
proposed.description: TL;DR QuePaxa is a consensus algorithm published in 2023 by Tennage, Băsescu and co-authors that lets a group of machines agree on an ordered log while any proposer can move the protocol forward. Cloudflare says it is building Meerkat, an experimental consensus service for its internal global control plane, on QuePaxa, in a post published on 11 November 2026. Leader-based algorithms such as Raft, Multi-Paxos and Viewstamped Replication recover by detecting a failed leader and electing a replacement, and that recovery path is where a wide-area network hurts most. QuePaxa keeps proposers cooperating: priorities are random, a proposer adopts any higher-priority proposal it meets, and clients hedge by sending a request to every replica. A round has four phases (propose and adopt, spread, check and decide, carry forward), and a proposer that misses the one-round-trip fast path carries its work into the next round. In Cloudflare's own Meerkat tests the decision rate fell to about 65% of its usual level while a failed leader was being replaced and returned to 100% a minute later; Cloudflare describes QuePaxa as less battle-tested than Raft and is formally verifying its implementation, so the open question is the evidence a buyer can inspect. The Cloudflare Research post at blog.cloudflare.com/choosing-quepaxa, retrieved 2026-11-12, which introduces Meerkat and explains why its authors
proposed.title: QuePaxa Lets a Global Control Plane Keep Deciding While Links Stall

proposed.author: Programming Central
proposed.description: A 266-line gate that rejects 5 of 7 rows before the engine sees them — a reason per row, a hash per artifact. A product feed with a few thousand SKUs always contains a handful of rows that cannot become a banner: a title that arrives as whitespace, a currency written usd , an image path with .. in it, a sale price above the price. None of these are design problems, and none of them fail where they happen — they fail twenty minutes later, as a command_batch error with no row number and a half-written PNG. The fix is not better error handling inside the render job. It is a gate that runs before the engine is involved at all, decides row by row, and writes down why. A row either has a reason to be rejected or it does not: that is the entire contract, and it makes the pipeline boring in the way a pipeline should be. This post is that gate — ten rejection rules, the ordering that matters, and the audit report that makes a rejected row a fact instead of a support ticket. proposed.description: The Register writes that "The worst of the patchpocalypse may be behind us, according to Linus Torvalds." In his weekly kernel update post, Torvalds said Linux 7.4 rc2 was a big release partly because it contained code he'd left out of rc1 because he'd been busy and it was already the largest such release in kernel history. But Torvalds said the other reason rc2 was big was "various AI fixes." Such fixes are necessary because ever since Anthropic launched its Mythos bug-finding model in April, developers have been able to find more software flaws than was previously possible. Microsoft, for example, addressed a record 974 flaws in September — its third record fixing spree this year after it whacked 622 flaws in July and 206 in June. Oracle addressed 1,449 flaws in a single month. That's many more patches than IT teams are set up to handle, yet they must find ways to deal with bugs more quickly because attackers are increasingly targeting flaws found by AI. Torvalds' post suggests that, perhaps, the worst of this is behind us. "This time around Alexei claims that on the bpf side at least the fixes are now coming in faster than the new reports, and that sounds lovely if true," he wrote. That's a reference to Alexei Starovoitov, co-creator and lead dev on the Extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF), the project that makes it possible to run sandboxed programs within the Linux kerne

proposed.description: A saved OpenRTB response can be valid JSON and still bid on an impression that was never offered. Once the originating request is discarded, the evidence needed to establish that relationship is gone. A replay fixture should preserve the request, response and interpretation context together. The pair lets you test relationships that neither document can establish independently. This walkthrough checks request identity, impression matching and response currency. The examples are deliberately incomplete fragments. They are not full OpenRTB validators or examples of auction-ready traffic. Keep the smallest useful pair Start with a request containing two impression IDs and an explicit allowed currency. Keep a response with one bid pointing to one of those impressions. Do not reduce the fixture to a response and a comment describing the request. Comments drift, while an executable relationship test can fail when an adapter changes a field. Preserve the OpenRTB specification snapshot, exchange profile, request headers relevant to interpretation and validator version beside the pair. A field's JSON type alone does not identify the contract under which the exchange processed it. For a historical failure, retain both a controlled original capture and a sanitized regression fixture. The latter should reproduce the relevant structure without carrying unnecessary production identifiers or
proposed.title: A replay fixture should keep the OpenRTB request beside the response.

proposed.author: Muhammad Azlaan Zubair
proposed.description: Imagine a developer reaches an interview with a polished resume full of ownership, impact and leadership claims. The interviewer asks what the developer personally changed and how the result was measured. The answers become vague: some bullets describe team outcomes as individual work; others have no evidence behind them. That is the wrong use of AI in a job search. A model can make weak evidence sound convincing, but it cannot give you experience. Use it to research roles, organise real examples, improve clarity and rehearse explanations. Keep every claim traceable to work you actually did. Where AI genuinely helps AI is useful when it helps turn authentic experience into a clear application. Treat it as an editor and practice partner—not the author of your professional history. 1. Decode a job description Ask AI to separate a job description into categories instead of merely summarising it. A useful analysis identifies: Core requirements: skills that appear central to the role's actual work. Supporting requirements: tools or practices that may help but are not the main job. Responsibilities: outcomes the role is expected to deliver. Evidence to prepare: projects or examples that could demonstrate each requirement. Unknowns: details the posting does not establish, such as team structure, deployment ownership or the exact level of production responsibility. A job description is
proposed.title: Using AI in Your Tech Job Search Without Faking Anything

proposed.author: BeauHD
proposed.description: An anonymous reader quotes a report from Reuters: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang misled several of the company's leaders, including general counsel Tim Teter and chief marketing officer Alison Wagonfeld, about the nature of his relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, with whom he had an affair, according to two people familiar with the matter and internal correspondence reviewed by Reuters. [...] During the autumn of 2025 and in October 2026, in response to press queries that drew some Nvidia leaders' attention to his relationship with Megaspeed and Alice Huang, Huang at both times described their interactions as appropriate, the people said, speaking on the condition of anonymity. Reuters only reviewed messages from the exchanges in October, not the ones from 2025. In two separate messages in October, Huang told Nvidia leaders, including Teter and Wagonfeld, that the interactions reflected standard business dealings with customers. In other messages, Huang affirmed the routine nature of his interactions with Megaspeed. Nvidia's Huang also discussed taking legal action against the New York Times after it published an article in October of last year that drew attention to his meetings in public with Alice Huang, the people said. That article had prompted Jensen Huang to communicate with some Nvidia leaders in 2025 about their interactions, which he did not describe
proposed.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Misled Company Leaders On Affair With Chinese Businesswoman

proposed.author: Miguel Dantas
proposed.description: The captain, the talisman, the brand: former teammates and experts discuss Portugal entering a new era after 23 years There are days football fans hope will never come. For Portugal, this is one of them. For 23 years, Cristiano Ronaldo has been more than the country’s greatest footballer; he has been its defining sporting figure, a symbol of national pride and constant presence in the lives of supporters. After 234 appearances and 146 goals, the No 7 brought that chapter to a close and on Saturday night the team will play their first game without him . The national side are losing more than a great footballer; they are also losing one of the world’s biggest brands. Daniel Sá, the executive director of the Portuguese institute of marketing administration, believes Portugal require reinvention to attract at least some of the millions of viewers who tuned in because of CR7. Continue reading...
proposed.title: Portugal did the extraordinary with Cristiano Ronaldo. Can they do it without him?
